author_answer: Root is correct. Space for one working drawing, one ordinary blank and one three-drawing continuation marker is sufficient for a first or last fragment line, but not a middle line of a word with at least two continued breaks. The original unconditional single-unit fallback statement omitted that second marker and blank.

unchanged_continuation_protocol.middle_fragment_line: marker, ordinary blank, nonempty fragment, ordinary blank, marker
unchanged_continuation_protocol.reading: The already specified matched line-edge markers join fragments into the same logical word before grammatical parsing. No marker, blank, empty fragment, source character or grammatical control is omitted.

fully_paid_width_condition: Measure available line width in the chosen teaching hand, without assuming equal-width native glyphs or a manuscript cell raster. Let M be the actual horizontal width needed to write the complete rr-ch marker, B the width of an ordinary visible word blank, and G the largest horizontal width of any one of the22working drawings in this hand.

A uniform sufficient condition for the single-drawing fallback on every line used by an arbitrarily long word is usable width at least2*M+2*B+G. This pays both markers and blanks on an intermediate line. It also provides enough space for a first or last fragment line, whose requirement is only M+B+G.

For a particular middle fragment containing one drawing g, the exact stated layout needs2*M+2*B+width(g); using G is the worst-case guarantee for any next working drawing. Longer fragments require their actual width instead of width(g).

In an optional equal-cell teaching display with one cell per working drawing and one per ordinary blank, a middle line needs at least nine cells: seven drawn units and two blanks. First/last fragment lines need five. These are illustration counts, not an imposed native raster or equal-width manuscript assumption.

If the current line lacks room for a first fragment and its marker, begin the continued word on a new suitable line. If a subsequent line or page is too narrow for the required middle layout, this format cannot guarantee writing the word; choose an adequate writing surface or report the physical format unsupported. Do not erase a marker, hide a boundary or treat an unmarked break as continuation.
cost_and_scope: Each continued break still costs exactly two three-drawing markers plus the two ordinary blanks already specified. A middle row belongs to two breaks and therefore carries both marker roles.
